findings.headline: The Variable Revenue Provision reserve is forecast to reach about £52m by the end of 2031/32.
findings.detail: The report says a net contribution of £8.5m goes into the VRP reserve in 2027/28, under the MRP policy approved in March 2024. It says the balance will be needed to pay for increased MRP costs in future years.
findings.matters: A reserve built to fund future minimum revenue provision is a specific debt-cost mechanism that finance officers elsewhere may use as a comparison point.
findings.figures: £52m (forecast VRP reserve by end 2031/32); £8.5m (2027/28 net contribution)
findings.quote: By the end of the 2031/32, the balance on the VRP reserve is forecast in the region of £52m.

findings.headline: Proposed release of £11.96m of uncommitted capital budget to assist treasury management.
findings.detail: The report also adds £0.415m of match-funded borrowing for a 3G pitch at Leeds Road, securing £1.7m of external funding. It says the investment programme reduces forecast debt.
findings.matters: Releasing uncommitted capital budget to support treasury management is a specific borrowing-related decision that other councils managing capital financing budgets may compare.
findings.figures: £11.96m (uncommitted capital budget released); £0.415m (match-funded borrowing); £1.7m (external funding)
findings.quote: Note the proposed release of £11.96m uncommitted budget across the multi-year capital plan to assist treasury management of the capital financing budget

findings.headline: The report says that without recognising ongoing pressures and reserve contributions, 'a S114 notice would remain a possibility'.
findings.detail: The report links the S114 risk to the robustness of the 2027/28 budget and its signing off by the S151 officer. It says the need for such a report will be kept under constant review depending on delivery of the savings proposals.
findings.matters: The report explicitly ties the S114 possibility to savings delivery, which is the variable a finance director or lender would watch in the year ahead.
findings.quote: a S114 notice would remain a possibility

findings.headline: A 4.99% council tax increase is assumed for 2027/28, adding £15.3m of income.
findings.detail: The increase comprises a 2.99% core council tax rise and a 2% adult social care precept. The report says a 1% reduction would reduce council tax funding by about £2.7m a year and that government will not fund any shortfall.
findings.matters: The council tax assumption is the largest single income increase in the budget, and any reduction would need to be met by further savings.
findings.figures: 4.99% (total increase); £15.3m (additional 2027/28 council tax income); £85.9m (over 5 years); £2.7m (cost of 1% reduction per annum)
findings.quote: The total amount of additional Council tax funding assumed in 2027/28 is £15.3m

findings.headline: The Collection Fund council tax deficit stood at £10.4m at 31 March 2026, with £7.2m to be repaid in 2027/28.
findings.detail: The 2026/27 budget repays £3.2m, and the remaining £7.2m is assumed to be part funded from a £4.0m drawdown from the Collection Fund Smoothing reserve. The report says the repayment amount may change once the 2026/27 year-end position is estimated in January 2027.
findings.matters: The deficit repayment depends on a smoothing reserve drawdown, which is a one-off funding source, and the final figure depends on January 2027 estimates.
findings.figures: £10.4m (Collection Fund deficit at 31 March 2026); £3.2m (repaid 2026/27); £7.2m (2027/28 repayment); £4.0m (smoothing reserve drawdown)
findings.quote: As at 31st March 2026 the total Collection Fund deficit was £10.4m

findings.headline: General reserves are expected to be £27.0m by March 2027, rising to £47m by 2032.
findings.detail: The report assumes no use of general reserves in 2026/27 and a revised annual contribution of £4m from 2028/29 onward. It says the risk assessment estimated a minimum value of risks at £28.5m.
findings.matters: Reserves rebuilding from £27.0m towards £47m over five years is central to the council's stated sustainability path, and the risk assessment figure gives a comparison point.
findings.figures: £27.0m (general reserves March 2027); £47m (general reserves 2032); £4m (revised annual contribution); £28.5m (minimum value of risks)
findings.quote: The general reserves are expected to be £27.0m by March 2027

findings.headline: The Council will receive a £73m government grant in November 2026 to write off 90% of the historic High Needs Block deficit.
findings.detail: The report says the DfE has indicated a 'proportionate' contribution towards in-year DSG deficits in 2026/27 and 2027/28, assumed at 90% but not confirmed. It also says the statutory override remains in place until March 2028.
findings.matters: The statutory override expiring in March 2028 and the unconfirmed 90% in-year contribution are the two points a lender or finance director would track on the DSG position.
findings.figures: £73m (grant to write off historic HNB deficit); 90% (write-off share); March 2028 (override end date)
findings.quote: The Council will receive a grant of £73m in November 2026 to write off 90% of the historic HNB deficit

findings.headline: Adults & Health's £2.6m income saving is considered not fully deliverable, so the income budget is reduced by £0.6m.
findings.detail: The report says the shortfall is partly due to the short-term nature of improvements in debt recovery, and partly to reduced resident capital affecting overall income. Savings previously approved for 2027/28 total £2.2m.
findings.matters: A previously budgeted saving being judged partly undeliverable is a sign of the pressure a council may face in converting savings into cash, which other finance officers will recognise.
findings.figures: £2.6m (previously budgeted saving); £0.6m (income reduction); £2.2m (previously approved Adults savings 2027/28); £5.2m (total Adults savings requirement 2027/28)
findings.quote: a previously budgeted saving of £2.6m which is considered not be fully deliverable

findings.headline: Children's services has a £7m Quarter 2 pressure on external placements, and the 2027/28 budget resets the base to 50 placements from 38.
findings.detail: The report says the pressure relates to the number and weekly cost of external placements for looked after children. Children's services also has £11.1m of demand-led funding for looked after children in 2027/28.
findings.matters: A reset of the placement base from 38 to 50 is a concrete demand assumption, and the report says the service is developing proposals to reduce numbers from that base.
findings.figures: c£7m (Quarter 2 pressure in 2026/27); 50 (revised base placements); 38 (current budget placements); £11.1m (looked after children demand funding 2027/28)
findings.quote: from the current budget of 38

findings.headline: Kirklees forecasts a £9.8m overspend for 2026/27 at Quarter 2, improved by £3.8m since Quarter 1.
findings.detail: The report says several pressures are expected to continue into 2027/28, particularly in social care. It also says early indications of the Quarter 3 position suggest the in-year overspend will reduce further.
findings.matters: A reader tracking in-year overspend recovery will want to compare the Quarter 2 figure with the Quarter 3 position the report says is being indicated.
findings.figures: £9.8m (2026/27 forecast overspend at Quarter 2); £3.8m (improvement since Quarter 1)
findings.quote: This has improved by £3.8m since Quarter 1

findings.headline: The 2027/28 proposals include £4.9m of staffing budget reductions through new savings, with £0.4m already removed from head of service posts.
findings.detail: The report says the reductions focus on vacant posts and back-office functions rather than frontline delivery. Total new savings for 2027/28 are stated as £15.0m, or £22.1m including previously agreed savings.
findings.matters: Staffing reductions of this size are a material part of the savings plan, and the report's own figures show new savings of £15.0m against a £22.1m total that depends on delivery.
findings.figures: £4.9m (staffing budget reduction 2027/28); £0.4m (senior management removed); £15.0m (new savings); £22.1m (total savings including previously agreed)
findings.quote: with a further £4.9m reduction in staffing budgets overall in 2027/28 through new savings proposals

findings.headline: Kirklees' forecast budget gap for 2027/28 is £1.0m, down from £24m in the October MTFS.
findings.detail: The report says the 2027/28 gap has been reduced through savings and pressure changes, with a further £3.1m gap in 2028/29. It says the gap will need resolving before a balanced budget is set in February 2027.
findings.matters: A council closing a £24m gap to £1.0m before the settlement is published shows how far the savings programme has moved the position, and the remaining gap depends on savings still to be delivered.
findings.figures: £24m (October MTFS gap for 2027/28); £1.0m (December gap 2027/28); £3.1m (2028/29)
findings.quote: The forecast budget gap for 2027/28 is currently £1.0m, with a further £3.1m in 2028/29

findings.headline: Agency reliance remains high in some technically specialist areas, currently engineering and legal
findings.detail: The Organisational resourcing risk update says the council continues to see high reliance on agency staff in technically specialist areas. Targeted work in those high-spend areas is ongoing, using different recruitment options to reduce spend.
findings.matters: Agency spend is a recurring cost premium that a finance director at another council compares against their own staffing budget, and is often the first place a staffing overspend appears.
findings.figures: no figures given
findings.quote: Continue to see a high reliance on agency staff in some technically specialist areas

findings.headline: Regulatory Notice removed from Housing Safety & Quality, with the risk score reduced to 9
findings.detail: The Regulator of Social Housing inspection recognised progress on the 2024 Regulatory Notice, including tenant health and safety, damp and mould, and repairs. The paper says the Notice has been removed and that a Regulatory Improvement Plan will go to Cabinet in Q3.
findings.matters: Removal of a regulatory notice from a housing service is a regulator's formal acknowledgement of improvement, and a lender to a council's housing company or HRA looks for exactly this kind of outcome.
findings.figures: risk score 9; 5-year Capital Investment Plan £160m
findings.quote: As a result, the Regulatory Notice has been removed.

findings.headline: Temporary accommodation households in B&B fell to 51, from 336 in TA overall at end of Q2
findings.detail: The Homelessness and temporary accommodation risk says the number of households in B&B has continued a positive downward trend. Zero families were in B&B at the end of Q2, and none were in B&B over six weeks during the quarter. The paper says housing supply and move-on accommodation remain major concerns.
findings.matters: Nightly-paid B&B is one of the most expensive forms of temporary accommodation, so a finance director would track whether a council's B&B count is falling against the TA total it still carries.
findings.figures: 336 in TA overall; 51 in B&B (households); Rough Sleeping Programme funding £470k for 2026/7
findings.quote: the number of households in B&B has continued a positive downward trend

findings.headline: Adult Social Care reports more complex people entering the service than leaving it
findings.detail: The Sustainability of Adult Social Care risk update says complexity of people requiring service has increased. Detailed analysis with Finance has strengthened understanding of the impact of price, volume and complexity, which is informing budget monitoring and planning.
findings.matters: Rising complexity of need, rather than volume alone, is what drives the cost of adult social care, and a finance director elsewhere would compare it with their own price, volume and complexity analysis.
findings.figures: no figures given
findings.quote: Complexity of people requiring service has increased with more complex people entering adult social care compared with those leaving

findings.headline: Budgetary pressures in Sufficiency of Children's Care are linked to reliance on external residential placements
findings.detail: The paper attributes current budgetary pressures in Sufficiency of Children's Care to reliance on external residential placements and increasing complexity of need. It says these are reflective of national trends and will be considered in MTFS development. Internal residential occupancy has risen to 20 of 22 places.
findings.matters: External residential placement costs are a major driver of children's social care overspends, and a finance director at another council will want to see how a peer is sizing this pressure in its forecast.
findings.figures: internal residential occupancy 20/22 available places; 74% of looked after children live in a family setting
findings.quote: Current budgetary pressures as a result of reliance on external residential placements and increasing complexity of need are reflective of national trends across the sector

findings.headline: Economic Growth and Regeneration risk notes that programme prolongation could challenge budgets across schemes
findings.detail: The paper says schemes are entering contract and delivery phases, but ongoing financial and operational challenges remain. Programme prolongation could challenge budgets across the schemes, and the Cultural Heart phase two completion is planned for Q4 2028.
findings.matters: A regeneration programme that is running longer than planned puts pressure on budgets for every scheme in it, a pattern a finance director at another council with a similar capital programme would recognise.
findings.figures: Cultural Heart phase two planned completion Q4 2028
findings.quote: Programme prolongation has the potential to challenge budgets across schemes.

findings.headline: Asset rationalisation is progressing well and is on track to meet its income target
findings.detail: The Corporate Assets portfolio risk update says building safety compliance levels continue to improve and that asset rationalisation is on track to meet its income target. An Asset Transformation project is underway following an Arcadis review, and the PPP expiry team needs additional funding for extra posts.
findings.matters: A council hitting an asset sales income target is a concrete funding source, and peers and lenders assess whether such income is replacing revenue or borrowing.
findings.figures: on track to meet income target (no figure given)
findings.quote: Asset rationalisation continues to progress well and on track to meet income target

findings.headline: External audit gave an unqualified opinion on 2024-25 accounts, and draft 2025-26 accounts were published on the statutory timetable
findings.detail: The Medium Term Financial Sustainability controls record that external audit of accounts is completed annually. The paper states the opinion on 2024-25 accounts was unqualified and that draft 2025-26 accounts were published in line with the statutory timetable.
findings.matters: An unqualified opinion and an on-time draft set of accounts are the audit outcomes a finance director at another council benchmarks against, and a lender looks for in assessing the council's financial reporting.
findings.figures: unqualified opinion on 2024-25 accounts
findings.quote: unqualified opinion provided on 2024-25 accounts

findings.headline: Procurement risk removed from the corporate register following implementation of the Procurement Act
findings.detail: The paper removes the Procurement risk (LGC03), citing the successful implementation of the Procurement Act and embedding of its requirements. Focus has shifted from process compliance to contract and supplier performance, which is now tracked under Contract Management (LGC04) and at Service level.
findings.matters: A council removing a procurement risk from its corporate register, while contract management stays on it, shows where a peer council's own control priorities are moving under the new Act.
findings.figures: 24 risks at end of Q2, down 1 from Q1
findings.quote: Procurement has been removed reflecting the successful implementation of the Procurement Act

findings.headline: Safety Valve arrangement ends on 1 April, with revised financial trajectories requiring DfE sign-off
findings.detail: The paper says the Safety Valve arrangement ends on 1 April. Revised financial trajectories and expectations form part of the DfE implementation planning, which will require DfE sign-off and then be subject to monitoring.
findings.matters: The end of a Safety Valve agreement, with new trajectories needing DfE approval, is a point where a council's High Needs deficit path is reset, and it is relevant to any council in a similar arrangement.
findings.figures: arrangement ends 1 April
findings.quote: Safety Valve arrangement end on 1st April with revised financial trajectories and expectations

findings.headline: Medium Term Financial Strategy provides funding to increase general reserves by £4m a year and reduce reliance on earmarked reserves
findings.detail: The paper states that the MTFS funds an increase in general reserves and reduces the council's reliance on earmarked reserves. It sits alongside the statement that significant pressures continue in Social Care and that savings will be required to balance the budget.
findings.matters: A council moving money from earmarked reserves into general reserves changes its reserve mix, which a finance director at another council or a lender would weigh against the pressures named in the same paper.
findings.figures: £4m pa to general reserves
findings.quote: The MTFS provides funding to increase the general reserves by £4m pa and reduces the reliance

findings.headline: Directorate savings target for 2027-28 is still to be established, per the Medium Term Financial Sustainability further actions
findings.detail: The further actions for the Medium Term Financial Sustainability risk include establishing directorate savings targets and agreeing action plans for 2027-28. The capital plan is also to be updated as part of the budget process, and the paper says further reductions will be required.
findings.matters: A council that has not yet set savings targets for the year after next has a gap between its stated need for savings and its named delivery plan, which a finance director at another council or a lender would want to see closed.
findings.figures: 2027-28 directorate savings targets
findings.quote: Directorate savings target to be established and action plans to be agreed for 2027-28

findings.headline: Budget monitoring risk scored 16 as budget overspends appeared within both Adults and Children's Services at end of Q2 2026-27
findings.detail: The paper reports increasing delivery risks to the agreed 2026-27 budget, citing overspends in both Adults and Children's Services at the end of Q2. It says additional 2026-27 funding for cost pressures may be insufficient to fully mitigate continued volatility in social care demand budgets.
findings.matters: Overspends in both social care directorates in the same year, and the council's own view that added funding may not cover them, is the kind of in-year pressure peers and lenders track.
findings.figures: risk score 16; overspends within both Adults and Children's Services at end of Q2 2026-27
findings.quote: as seen by the budget overspends within both Adults and Children

findings.headline: Medium Term Financial Sustainability risk rises to a score of 15, red, from amber, with impact raised from 4 to 5
findings.detail: The paper says the increase reflects the position in the Medium-Term Financial Strategy during Q2. It states that setting a balanced budget will require significant savings across current and future years, with focus remaining on social care budget pressures.
findings.matters: A finance director needs to know the council's own risk register now rates its medium-term financial sustainability as red and expects significant savings to balance future budgets.
findings.figures: risk score 15; impact score from 4 to 5
findings.quote: The setting of a balanced budget will require identification of significant savings, across both current and future financial years.

findings.headline: DfE approved Kirklees' DSG management plan, with funding for 90% of the High Needs deficit to be received during Q3
findings.detail: The paper says DfE approved the council's Dedicated Schools Grant management plan submission. Confirmation of a successful submission will result in Kirklees receiving 90% funding to address the High Needs deficit. The Safety Valve arrangement ends on 1 April.
findings.matters: A council with a High Needs deficit is watching whether DfE accepts its DSG recovery plan, and a 90% funding share for that deficit is a concrete, reportable outcome for peers in the same position.
findings.figures: 90% of the High Needs deficit to be funded in Q3
findings.quote: DfE have approved our Dedicated Schools Grant (DSG) management plan submission, with the result that funding for 90% of the High Needs deficit to be received during Q3

findings.matters: Procurements that narrow to two bidders, alongside adviser cost pressure, affect value-for-money outcomes that other councils running waste contracts will face.

findings.matters: A falling looked-after population with a higher share in family settings is a placement-cost trend that peers managing high-cost placements will compare against.

findings.quote: In terms of the £250k saving incorporated into the Adults Directorate 2026/27 budget, cashable savings are anticipated to be realised during Q3 and Q4.

findings.matters: Reserve carry-forward requests signal that committed spend crosses financial years, which affects how other councils plan their reserve drawdowns.

findings.matters: A stated gap between a funded replacement plan and the whole-fleet cost is a direct capital planning exposure that peers with ageing fleets will recognise.
