findings.matters: Treasury savings created by capital slippage, rather than by a planned borrowing change, are a link between capital delivery and revenue budgets that finance officers elsewhere will recognise.
findings.figures: £4.3m Central Budgets underspend; £2.5m Treasury Management; £1.2m energy; £0.2m superannuation
findings.quote: At Quarter 2 there is a projected underspend of £ 4.3m in Central Budgets. Of this, £2.5m sits within Treasury Management and is related to slippage in the capital plan since the budget was approved.

findings.headline: Kirklees reports the 2026/27 capital budget revised to £256.5m at Q2, with £8.2m of slippage reprofiled into future years
findings.detail: The paper reports General Fund slippage of £10.8m offset by £2.4m of grant allocations, and HRA acceleration of £2.7m. The multi-year capital plan now stands at £1.173bn, with the Woodley School and College, the George Hotel redevelopment and the Cultural Heart Programme among the slipped schemes.
findings.matters: Capital slippage of this scale is a pattern peers will compare against their own delivery, and the paper says future capital plans will face more scrutiny and reductions given the revenue position.
findings.figures: £256.5m revised 2026/27 capital budget; £8.2m slippage into future years; £10.8m General Fund slippage; £2.4m grant increase; £1.173bn multi-year plan
findings.quote: The Council's revised capital budget at Quarter 2 for 2026/27 is £256.5m.

findings.headline: Kirklees forecasts a £29.0m in-year DSG deficit at Q2 2026/27, with the Safety Valve contributions no longer in place
findings.detail: The paper attributes the in-year High Needs deficit to rising complexity in mainstream schools and above-funding inflationary increases from Independent Non-Maintained Special Schools providers. It says Cluster Working and more robust contract management are expected to stabilise costs over time.
findings.matters: An in-year high-needs deficit continuing after Safety Valve funding ends is a pressure other councils with SEND deficits will need to model.
findings.figures: £29.0m forecast in-year DSG deficit; £36m expected HNB deficit at March 2028
findings.quote: The Quarter 2 2026/27 position on the Dedicated Schools Grant (DSG) is a forecasted in-year deficit of £29.0m.

findings.headline: Government to fund 90% of Kirklees' £80.3m historic DSG deficit, with the Council receiving £73m in late November 2026 and estimating a c£13m contribution to March 2028
findings.detail: The paper says the DfE approved the Council's plan after the Safety Valve programme ended in February 2026, and the Council will receive £73m to write off the historic deficit. The Council's own share is estimated at c£13m, funded in the MTFS, and the paper says this will improve cash flow and allow Treasury Management savings.
findings.matters: Government write-off of 90% of a historic DSG deficit after the Safety Valve ended is a specific, recent arrangement that other councils with high-needs deficits will be tracking.
findings.figures: £80.3m historic DSG deficit; c£73m government funding; c£13m Council contribution to March 2028; £36m expected HNB deficit at March 2028
findings.quote: The Council has recently been informed of its approval and will receive a sum of £73m towards writing off the historic deficit in late November 2026.

findings.headline: Kirklees attributes £8.7m of its £9.8m forecast overspend to slippage and non-delivery of approved savings
findings.detail: The paper states that the majority of the forecast overspend relates to savings not being delivered, with a further £1.1m of net overspend on business-as-usual activity. Adults and Health savings brought forward from prior years show a forecast shortfall of £5.0m.
findings.matters: Savings non-delivery as the main driver of an overspend is a risk other councils running savings programmes will recognise, and it bears on whether future-year MTFS savings assumptions are credible.
findings.figures: £8.7m savings slippage and non-delivery; £1.1m net business-as-usual overspend; £5.0m forecast shortfall on brought-forward Adults savings
findings.quote: an estimated £8.7m is due to slippage and non-delivery of the approved savings programme across the Council

findings.headline: Kirklees reports Adults and Health and Children and Families directorates projecting a combined £14.7m overspend after budget contingency reserve
findings.detail: The paper attributes the overspend mainly to additional demand, rising complexity and delayed savings delivery, and says the 2026/27 budget added £15.2m for adults and £5.5m for children's care cost pressures. It also says the remaining directorates are relatively stable.
findings.matters: Social care demand-led overspends are a common pressure, and the scale of the figure against specific budget uplifts gives peers a concrete benchmark for their own care cost forecasts.
findings.figures: £14.7m combined projected overspend; £15.2m additional adults funding; £5.5m additional children's funding
findings.quote: Adults and Health and Children and Families Directorates are now projecting a combined overspend of £14.7m (after applying the budget contingency reserve).

findings.headline: Kirklees forecasts a £9.8m General Fund overspend at Q2 2026/27 after a £5.2m drawdown from the strategic budget contingency reserve, down from £13.6m at Q1
findings.detail: The paper reports the Q2 overspend improved by £3.8m since Q1, with the Council stating that reductions in employee spend and a £1.5m treasury saving from capital profiling contributed. The paper says the overspend is still considered probable at year end, which would require reserves to balance.
findings.matters: A finance director at another council can compare the trajectory of an in-year overspend recovery against their own, and a lender sees that year-end balance may depend on reserve drawdowns that must then be replenished.
findings.figures: £9.8m forecast overspend (Q2); £13.6m (Q1); £5.2m contingency reserve used; £3.8m improvement
findings.quote: the Council is forecast overspend of £9.8m after the use of the strategic budget contingency reserve of £5.2m

findings.headline: Equal pay claims received, with their validity and magnitude yet to be determined
findings.detail: The paper reports that the Council has received Equal Pay claims and that their validity and magnitude have not yet been determined. The auditor notes that if successful, the claims could pose a material challenge to financial sustainability.
findings.matters: Equal pay exposure of unknown size is a contingent liability that any council or lender assessing a metropolitan authority would want to understand.
findings.figures: None quantified in the paper
findings.quote: the validity and magnitude of these claims has yet to be determined

findings.headline: Non-ringfenced government funding up by around £14m in 2026-27
findings.detail: The paper reports that changes to central government funding have increased non-ringfenced funding for metropolitan councils, allowing more resources to be allocated to the areas under greatest pressure. The 2026-27 budget also allocated £15.2m to adult social care and £5.5m to children and families.
findings.matters: An increase in non-ringfenced funding after the Fair Funding 2.0 review is the funding change other metropolitan councils will be comparing their own settlements against.
findings.figures: around £14m increase in non-ringfenced funding in 2026-27; £15.2m additional adult social care; £5.5m additional children and families
findings.quote: the Council has seen an increase in non-ringfenced funding of around £14m in 2026-27

findings.headline: General fund financing costs of £41.3m in 2025-26, rising to £64.4m by 2029-30
findings.detail: The paper reports the general fund cost of borrowing as a share of the net revenue stream, which is expected to increase over the period. It notes the auditor treats the cost of borrowing as a significant financial pressure.
findings.matters: The rising cost of borrowing as a share of the revenue budget is the measure lenders and finance directors use to judge affordability.
findings.figures: £41.3m general fund financing costs 2025-26; £64.4m in 2029-30; 10.2% of net revenue stream in 2025-26 rising to 11% in 2029-30
findings.quote: The general fund financing costs in 2025-26 were £41.3m set to increase to £64.4m in 2029-30.

findings.headline: Leader elected in July 2026 at the third attempt, after a period with no Leader
findings.detail: The paper reports that following the May 2026 election, members were unable to elect a Leader for a period. The Chief Executive exercised Leader functions in the interim under the Constitution, including approving the June 2026 financial outturn report.
findings.matters: A council operating without an elected Leader for a period, with decisions taken by the Chief Executive, is a governance arrangement other councils may need to plan for.
findings.figures: Leader elected July 2026 at third attempt
findings.quote: A Leader was duly elected in July 2026, at the third attempt.

findings.headline: Housing regulator inspection in June/July 2026 led to a C3 consumer grade
findings.detail: The paper reports that the Regulator of Social Housing confirmed the 2024 regulatory notice would be lifted, but that the June/July 2026 inspection led to an overall C3 grade. The auditor has issued a new Key Recommendation on this, with the final action due by 31 October 2028.
findings.matters: Regulatory grading of housing services is a live issue for any council with a housing revenue account, and a new Key Recommendation follows the grade.
findings.figures: C3 consumer grade; 41% of homes surveyed by November 2026 (up from 25% at inspection); full stock survey coverage forecast by September 2027; final action due 31 October 2028
findings.quote: The Council received an inspection from the Regulator of Social Housing in June/July 2026

findings.headline: Internal audit delivered 55% of the 2025-26 audit plan
findings.detail: The paper reports that internal audit recruitment difficulties reduced the breadth and depth of coverage, and that the Head of Internal Audit's opinion was based on just sufficient evidence. It notes recent successful recruitment to some posts in 2026/27.
findings.matters: Internal audit capacity shortfalls can limit the assurance behind an annual opinion, a risk any council facing similar recruitment pressure would recognise.
findings.figures: 55% of the 2025-26 audit plan delivered
findings.quote: Only 55% of the 2025-26 audit plan was delivered.

findings.headline: Audit misstatements recurred on double counting of grant income and under-accrual of capital expenditure
findings.detail: The paper reports that the same misstatement types recurred, with gross internal area data errors reported in the last three ISA 260 reports. It states the auditor strongly recommends work on these areas before the 2026/27 closedown.
findings.matters: Recurring capital accounting errors across several audit cycles are a finance-function issue that other councils with similar capital programmes can check their own closedown against.
findings.figures: Gross internal area errors reported in last three ISA 260 reports
findings.quote: misstatements recurred on double counting of grant income and under-accrual of capital expenditure.

findings.headline: Draft financial statements found no adjustments to useable reserves, with an unmodified audit opinion expected
findings.detail: The paper reports that the audit identified no adjustments affecting useable reserves and that the audit completed to an earlier timetable than in the prior two years. The auditor expects an unmodified opinion, to be issued by the end of November 2026.
findings.matters: A finance director comparing audit experience at peer councils will note the absence of reserve adjustments and the earlier timetable.
findings.figures: No adjustments to useable reserves; audit opinion expected by end of November 2026
findings.quote: We did not identify any adjustments impacting on the Council's useable reserves balances which represents a good outcome for the Council.

findings.headline: Plan to increase total usable reserves to over £105m by 2030, from £61m in March 2025
findings.detail: The paper reports the Council's MTFS plan to rebuild usable reserves, including a £3.8m contribution to the Budget Contingency Reserve in 2026-27 and a Transformation Reserve increase. It notes the auditor's view that realising the increase depends on avoiding unplanned overspends.
findings.matters: A stated reserve rebuild target with dated milestones is the kind of plan other councils rebuilding from low reserves will compare against.
findings.figures: £61m usable reserves at March 2025; over £105m by 2030; £3.8m Budget Contingency Reserve contribution in 2026-27, rising to £5m a year from 2027-28; £1.7m Transformation Reserve increase
findings.quote: as part of an overall plan to increase total usable reserves in excess of £105m (based on 2027-28 draft budget proposals) by 2030, compared to £61m in March 2025.

findings.headline: Unallocated general reserves of £26.0m at 31 March 2026, 5.6% of the 2026-27 net revenue budget
findings.detail: The paper reports the unallocated general reserves balance and a separate usable general fund balance, which rose by £1m in 2025-26. It notes the Council plans to increase reserves by £4m per annum for the next five years.
findings.matters: Reserves as a percentage of net revenue budget is the measure the paper benchmarks against English metropolitan boroughs, so it is directly comparable across councils.
findings.figures: £26.0m unallocated general reserves (5.6% of 2026-27 net revenue budget); £62.5m usable general fund balances at 31 March 2026 (12.7%); £61.1m at 31 March 2025; £1m increase in 2025-26
findings.quote: The Council's unallocated General Reserves balance was £26.0m at 31 March 2026

findings.headline: DSG deficit of £80.3m at 31 March 2026, with 90% of the residual deficit to be received in November 2026
findings.detail: The paper reports the High Needs Block deficit rising in 2025-26 and the DfE's agreed Local SEND Reform Plan. It notes that the level of DfE support for 2026-27 and 2027-28 remains uncertain, and that the Council has assumed 90% support.
findings.matters: Deficit funding from central government at a stated percentage, with later years uncertain, is a live question for every council carrying a DSG deficit.
findings.figures: £80.3m DSG deficit at 31 March 2026; £17.5m increase in 2025-26 (27%); 90% support assumed; £12.9m residual balance projected at 31 March 2028
findings.quote: the Council will receive 90% of the 2025-26 residual deficit (£80.3m) in November 2026

findings.headline: Capital expenditure of £209m in 2025-26, 95% of the planned budget
findings.detail: The paper reports capital spend against the revised 2025-26 budget, with projects deferred into future years. It also reports that the Housing Revenue Account overspent by £1.5m due to increased activity on essential fire safety works.
findings.matters: Delivery against a revised capital budget, alongside a named HRA overspend, shows how one council's programme performed against plan.
findings.figures: £209m capital expenditure; £219.7m revised budget; 95%; HRA overspend £1.5m
findings.quote: Capital expenditure in 2025-26 totalled £209m; equivalent to 95% of the planned budget.

findings.headline: £57.7m of borrowing removed from the capital plan, with a further £37.4m identified for removal
findings.detail: The paper reports two rounds of reductions to planned borrowing, one based on the 2025 MTFS and one reported in October 2026. It notes the paper's own statement that all capital programmes remain under review, including alternative funding sources.
findings.matters: Reductions to borrowing-funded capital are a specific lever other councils with high borrowing have used, and the figures show how much was removed.
findings.figures: £57.7m removed (2025 MTFS); £37.4m identified for removal (October 2026)
findings.quote: In total £57.7m of borrowing was removed from the capital plan, based on the 2025 MTFS, with a further £37.4m identified for removal, reported in October 2026.

findings.headline: Council borrowing forecast to rise from £817m at 31 March 2026 to £1,048m by 31 March 2029
findings.detail: The paper sets out the increase in external borrowing needed to deliver the planned capital programme, split between general fund and HRA. It states that these amounts are within the Council's affordable borrowing limits but are moving closer to them.
findings.matters: A forecast rise of this size, moving toward affordable limits, is the borrowing trajectory lenders and other councils with large capital programmes will track.
findings.figures: £817m external borrowing at 31 March 2026 (general fund £658m; HRA £159m); £1,048m forecast at 31 March 2029 (general fund £790m; HRA £258m)
findings.quote: The Council's borrowing is expected to increase from £817m (general fund £658m and Housing Revenue Account (HRA) £159m) on 31 March 2026 to £1,048m (general fund £790m and HRA £258m) on 31 March 2029

findings.headline: Quarter 2 2026-27 forecast overspend of £9.8m, down from £13.5m at quarter 1
findings.detail: The paper reports the in-year forecast improving between quarters 1 and 2, with the largest forecast overspends in Children and Families and Adults and Health. It also reports a quarter 2 savings shortfall of £8.7m.
findings.matters: A movement in the in-year forecast from quarter 1 to quarter 2 shows whether mitigations are working, which is the test peers and lenders apply during a year.
findings.figures: £9.8m quarter 2 forecast overspend; £13.5m quarter 1 forecast; £8.7m quarter 2 savings shortfall
findings.quote: the Council at quarter 2 forecasting an overspend of £9.8m reducing from £13.5m at quarter 1

findings.headline: Adults and Health and Children and Families overspent by £21.6m combined in 2025-26
findings.detail: The paper reports that the two demand-led directorates overspent by a combined sum that was offset by underspends in central budgets, including treasury management savings. It attributes the pattern to increasing demand and under-delivery of recurrent savings.
findings.matters: Demand-led social care overspends of this kind are widely shared across English councils, so the offset mechanism is useful for peers to compare.
findings.figures: £21.6m combined overspend; £5.5m contingency reserve
findings.quote: the Children and Families and Adults and Health directorates overspent by some £21.6m

findings.headline: Savings delivered of £19.2m against a £30.2m target (64%) in 2025-26
findings.detail: The paper reports that directorate savings of £18.4m were delivered against a target of £26.9m, excluding prior-year slippage. It also reports that only £0.8m of prior-year slipped savings were delivered against a £3.4m target.
findings.matters: Savings under-delivery is the mechanism the auditor links to the carry-forward of savings into later budgets, which is relevant to any council running a similar savings programme.
findings.figures: £19.2m delivered; £30.2m target; 64%; £18.4m directorate savings delivered against £26.9m target; £0.8m prior-year slipped savings delivered against £3.4m
findings.quote: In 2025-26, the Council delivered £19.2m of savings - 64% of the £30.2m target.

findings.headline: Net revenue overspend of £1.8m in 2025-26, down from £5.6m in 2024-25
findings.detail: The Council reports a net revenue overspend for 2025-26 that is smaller than the prior year. The paper notes that underneath this, overspending in demand-led services increased, offset by other measures, many non-recurrent, and by the full £5.5m contingency reserve.
findings.matters: A finance director at another council can compare a headline outturn improvement against the underlying demand-led overspend that the same offsets were covering.
findings.figures: £1.8m net revenue overspend 2025-26; £5.6m overspend 2024-25; £5.5m contingency reserve used
findings.quote: The Council reported a net revenue overspend of £1.8m in 2025-26, an improvement on the £5.6m overspend in 2024-25.

findings.headline: Contract and project management arrangements, first reported in 2024/25, have been completed, with a final contract management report due to the Committee in January 2027.
findings.detail: The paper says best practice was identified, a training package and framework were rolled out, and a Contract Register dashboard was shared with Service Leadership Teams. The paper also states that some concerns persist in contract management, data and information management, and cash handling.
findings.matters: Contract management was a repeated audit concern, and the paper's move from in-progress to completed status is the change a finance director at a similar council would look for.
findings.figures: January 2027 (final contract management report to CGAC)
findings.quote: Contract and project management arrangements, first reported in 2024/25 has also been completed.

findings.headline: No Leader or Cabinet was appointed between May and July 2026, with interim arrangements giving decision-making responsibility to the Chief Executive in consultation with Group Leaders.
findings.detail: The paper says the absence of agreement between political parties led to the inability to appoint a Leader and Cabinet. A Cabinet has since been formed, and three meeting cycles have occurred since.
findings.matters: A period without a Leader or Cabinet, with decisions taken under interim arrangements, is a governance position other councils and lenders would want to understand.
findings.figures: May to July 2026 (period without a Leader and Cabinet); three meeting cycles (since appointment)
findings.quote: which led to the inability to appoint a Leader and Cabinet between May and July 2026

findings.headline: The 2024/25 financial statements received an unqualified opinion, and the external auditor's value for money review retained three key recommendations from the previous year.
findings.detail: The paper says the auditor noted positive improvements in the Council's overall financial position and expects these to be reflected in the 2025/26 report. The external auditor continued to identify financial sustainability, SEND and housing regulatory issues as valid at the end of 2025/26.
findings.matters: An unqualified opinion alongside retained VFM recommendations, with the auditor noting improvement, is the external assurance position a lender or peer finance team would weigh.
findings.figures: three key recommendations (retained from the previous year)
findings.quote: The 2024/25 financial statements, approved in January 2026, received an unqualified opinion

findings.headline: Following the inspection in summer 2026, the Council received a C3 judgement, which replaced the March 2024 Regulatory Notice.
findings.detail: The paper says the judgement identified failings in stock condition, decency and anti-social behaviour. A service improvement plan has been put in place with resources identified. The original five-year low-rise fire programme has been accelerated, with fire door and compartmentation contracts awarded in October 2026.
findings.matters: A regulatory judgement on housing stock, along with the resource commitment and accelerated programme that follows, is a risk any council with a large housing revenue account would track.
findings.figures: C3 (regulatory judgement); February 2028 (anticipated completion of low-rise programme, as stated in the paper)
findings.quote: Following the inspection in summer 2026, the Council received a C3 judgement

findings.headline: The 2026/27 capital plan was revised from an initial budgeted expenditure of £315m to £262.3m in the MTFS refresh.
findings.detail: The paper states the initial 2026/27 capital budget covered General Fund and Housing Revenue Account expenditure and was revised down in the MTFS refresh. Work is ongoing to develop a sustainable capital plan for the December budget report.
findings.matters: A reduction of around £52.7m in a single year's capital plan shows how a council is adjusting its programme to remain affordable, which bears on borrowing need and funding.
findings.figures: £315m (initial 2026/27 budgeted capital expenditure, GF plus HRA); £262.3m (revised figure)
findings.quote: This was revised down to £262.3m in the MTFS refresh.

findings.headline: The MTFS budget gap for 2027/28 was £24m, which the draft budget proposals have in the main addressed, subject to Council approval in February 2027.
findings.detail: The paper says the MTFS was reviewed and updated in October 2026 to cover 2027/28 to 2031/32. The draft 2027/28 budget will be presented to Cabinet in December 2026 with new savings proposals.
findings.matters: A stated gap for the coming year, and the savings package intended to close it, is the key test of a council's medium-term position.
findings.figures: £24m (2027/28 budget gap per MTFS); 2027/28 to 2031/32 (MTFS period); February 2027 (budget approval)
findings.quote: The budget gap per the MTFS for 27/28 was £24m.

findings.headline: Quarterly reports note the need to further use reserves in the short term to balance the budget.
findings.detail: The paper states that quarterly reports to the Executive Leadership Team and Members have highlighted the in-year financial position and the need to use reserves to balance the budget in the short term.
findings.matters: Reliance on reserves to balance the in-year budget is a position a lender or finance director would want to see alongside the reserve balances themselves.
findings.quote: the need to further use reserves in the short term to balance the budget

findings.headline: Savings delivery at Q2 was 59% of the planned savings being achieved in year.
findings.detail: The paper reports savings delivery against plan at the Q2 point. Savings are tracked each month as part of the suite of corporate reports.
findings.matters: The share of planned savings delivered at mid-year indicates whether the savings assumptions in a budget are holding, which other councils with similar programmes can benchmark against.
findings.figures: 59% (planned savings achieved in year at Q2)
findings.quote: Savings delivery at Q2 is 59% of the planned savings

findings.headline: The projected overspend at the end of Q2 was £9.8m.
findings.detail: The paper says the Q2 projected overspend has been considered as part of the MTFP refresh in October 2026. It also states that there remain significant pressures in social care. The 2026/27 budget provides additional funding for demand pressures and for services that overspent.
findings.matters: A Q2 revenue overspend of this size, alongside social care pressures, shows the in-year position a finance director would track against the budget set for the year.
findings.figures: £9.8m (projected overspend at end of Q2)
findings.quote: The projected overspend of £9.8m at the end of Q2 has been considered as part of the MTFP refresh in October 2026.

findings.headline: A £73m payment from the High Needs Stability Grant is expected in November 2026, covering 90% of the historical SEND deficit, with the Council responsible for the remaining 10%.
findings.detail: The paper says the Safety Valve Programme would end and the DfE would pay off 90% of the DSG deficit during 2026 through the High Needs Stability Grant. The grant is now confirmed, and the Council expects to meet the remaining 10%, which the refreshed MTFS has set aside funds for.
findings.matters: Government grant covering most of a legacy DSG deficit, with the remainder funded by the council, is a funding model other councils with SEND deficits will be watching.
findings.figures: £73m (expected payment, November 2026); 90% (DfE share); 10% (Council share); March 2028 (override end)
findings.quote: This grant has been confirmed and a payment of £73m is expected in November 2026.

findings.headline: The SEND deficit within the Dedicated Schools Grant was £81.3m at 31 March 2026, up from £63.8m at 31 March 2025.
findings.detail: The paper states the deficit at 31 March 2026 and the prior-year comparator. It says the Statutory override, which allows the deficit to be classed as an Unusable Deficit reserve, ends in March 2028. The in-year 2026/27 deficit was projected at £29m at Q2.
findings.matters: A finance director at another council with a DSG deficit can compare the size, trajectory and the March 2028 override end date against their own position.
findings.figures: £81.3m (31 March 2026); £63.8m (31/3/25); £29m (2026/27 in-year deficit projected at Q2); March 2028 (override end)
findings.quote: The deficit at 31st March 2026 was £81.3m

findings.headline: Data Sharing & Security: further training across all services is required before information asset owners can sign off agreements.
findings.detail: Latest progress was reported to the October 2026 Information Governance Board, chaired by the Senior Information Risk Officer. The paper says the remaining work depends on training for information asset owners across all services.
findings.matters: Information governance weaknesses in data sharing carry legal and operational risk, and a finance director in another council may be dealing with the same training gap.
findings.figures: 2 fundamental recommendations (both partially complete); 4 significant recommendations (3 complete, 1 partially complete)
findings.quote: Further training is required across all Services to ensure information asset owners understand the requirement

findings.headline: Highway Accident Damage Recovery software replacement has a supplier confirmed, but the paper states that detailed timescales have yet to be established.
findings.detail: The replacement application is part of the Operational Services Asset Management System procurement and is in design and implementation. Further work on reporting lines is paused until the new system's requirements are clarified.
findings.matters: A system replacement with no set completion date, and with related recovery work paused, is the kind of open-ended IT commitment other councils will want to compare against their own timelines.
findings.figures: 3 of 4 significant recommendations outstanding (3 partially complete, 0 complete); 2 of these relate to highways management
findings.quote: Detailed timescales have yet to be established.

findings.headline: Clients' Property Register: four of six properties with outstanding key-storage recommendations have been sold, with the other two sales expected by March 2027.
findings.detail: The remaining recommendation concerns the storage and records of keys for properties to be sold. Management expects the final two sales, and full implementation, by March 2027.
findings.matters: Property disposals are a source of capital receipts, and the timing of the last two sales is a deadline a finance director can check.
findings.figures: 4 of 6 properties sold; 2 pending by March 2027
findings.quote: has been complied with regarding four of six properties which have now been sold

findings.headline: Guaranteed Hours Relief Cleaners recommendations: three business cases approved to progress, with the new management structure still to be implemented.
findings.detail: The management structure and working practices have been reviewed, producing three business cases covering relief arrangements, training/compliance and management restructuring. The remaining priority is implementing the new structure and carrying out a post-implementation review.
findings.matters: A staffing restructure approved in a service with five fundamental recommendations shows how a council is addressing a people and control issue, which other finance officers may be tracking.
findings.figures: Relief Cleaners: 13 significant recommendations (9 complete, 4 partially complete); 5 fundamental (4 complete, 1 partially complete)
findings.quote: three business cases covering relief arrangements, training/compliance and management restructuring, which have been approved to progress

findings.headline: Business rates liability audit trail improvements are due by end December 2026, with the small business relief review not starting until after April 2027.
findings.detail: The paper says the audit trail work will be complete in time for the discretionary relief review, but that testing for management assurance has taken considerable time. It also says the revised small business relief forms go live in November 2026, while the review of the large SBR caseload waits until after April 2027.
findings.matters: Business rates relief and liability controls bear directly on the income a council collects and whether it can rely on its records, which is of interest to finance directors and to lenders.
findings.figures: SBR review not until after April 2027; audit trail completion by end December 2026; forms live November 2026
findings.quote: there will not be any review exercise until after April 2027

findings.headline: 42 (64%) of the 66 significant audit recommendations due by 30 September 2026 are reported as complete, with 22 in progress.
findings.detail: The paper attributes the outstanding actions partly to management under-estimating realistic completion timescales, especially where IT and Data & Insight support is needed. One report is awaiting a management update.
findings.matters: The stated cause, under-estimated timescales for corporate enabler support, is a pattern other councils running similar action plans may recognise.
findings.figures: 42 of 66 significant recommendations complete (64%); 22 in progress; 1 awaiting management update
findings.quote: The remaining 22 are in progress, with only one report awaiting management update.

findings.headline: Four of seven fundamental audit recommendations due by 30 September 2026 are reported complete, with management status updates for the other three.
findings.detail: The paper classes any single fundamental recommendation as leading to a Limited Assurance opinion. Of the seven fundamental recommendations due, three are reported as partially complete, all in Public Health & Corporate Resources (Data Sharing & Security) and Place (Guaranteed Hours Relief Cleaners).
findings.matters: Fundamental recommendations drive assurance opinions, and a finance director here or at another council can compare the completion rate against their own tracker.
findings.figures: 4 of 7 fundamental recommendations complete; 3 partially complete
findings.quote: of the seven fundamental recommendations due to be completed by 30 September, four have been completed

findings.headline: General fund reserves were £62m at 31 March 2026, of which £26m was unearmarked, equal to 6.5% of the 2025/26 net revenue budget of £396m.
findings.detail: The auditor uses these reserves in its assessment of the expenditure fraud risk. It notes that the 6.5% exceeds the broad 5% sector target.
findings.matters: Unearmarked reserves at 6.5% of net revenue budget, above the 5% sector target, are a benchmark finance directors compare against their own cushions.
findings.figures: £62m general fund reserves; £26m unearmarked; 6.5% of £396m net revenue budget; 5% sector target
findings.quote: the Council had £62m of general fund reserves at 31 March 2026, of which £26m was unearmarked, equivalent to 6.5% of the 2025/26 net revenue budget of £396m.

findings.headline: The Council's LGPS net pension surplus of £0.85bn was capped at £nil under IFRIC 14 at 31 March 2026.
findings.detail: The asset ceiling reduces gross assets by £0.85bn, and the net balance is recognised at £nil. The auditor says the approach is consistent with the 2024/25 accounts.
findings.matters: The IFRIC 14 asset ceiling on a large surplus shows how much of an LGPS surplus a council can recognise on its balance sheet.
findings.figures: £0.85bn net LGPS surplus capped to £nil; £2.85bn gross asset; £2bn gross liability; £46m unfunded liabilities
findings.quote: At 31 March 2026, the Council identified a net LGPS pension surplus of £0.85bn, which was capped at £nil under IFRIC 14 by reducing gross assets by £0.85bn.

findings.headline: The audit has not yet concluded on management's response on equal pay, including the latest external legal advice.
findings.detail: This is one of the outstanding matters listed before the opinion can be issued. The auditor is awaiting management's response and the latest external legal advice.
findings.matters: An open equal pay exposure is a contingent liability that lenders and finance directors would want quantified.
findings.figures: none
findings.quote: obtaining and assessing management's response on equal pay, including the latest external legal advice;

findings.headline: The 2025/26 audit was completed to an earlier timetable than in the preceding two years, ahead of the revised 30 November 2027 accounts backstop date.
findings.detail: The auditor credits improvements to the cash flow statement working papers for the earlier close. Recurring capital accounting recommendations are still open and are expected to be addressed before the 2026/27 close.
findings.matters: An earlier audit close against a revised backstop date is a benchmark other councils can measure their own closedown against.
findings.figures: 30 November 2027 revised accounts backstop date
findings.quote: we have completed the work to an earlier timetable than in the preceding two years.

findings.headline: Grant income and non-pay expenditure were each overstated by £9.3m because DSG High Needs funding was double counted, with no net effect on the deficit outturn.
findings.detail: The auditor concluded the error arose from error rather than fraud. The adjustment has been made in the statements.
findings.matters: A double count in high-needs grant is a specific classification risk that DSG-deficit councils would want to check for in their own grant accounting.
findings.figures: £9.3m overstatement of grant income; £9.3m overstatement of non-pay expenditure
findings.quote: Our testing of grant income identified that Dedicated Schools Grant (DSG) High Needs funding had been double counted, overstating income by £9.3m.

findings.headline: Errors in gross internal area data have been reported in the last three ISA260 reports, with an extrapolated net error of £1m on assets valued at depreciated replacement cost.
findings.detail: The auditor found variances when agreeing valuer data to CAD drawings. The 2023/24 recommendation has been regraded as high priority and retained, because the issue has not been addressed.
findings.matters: A recurring audit recommendation on valuation source data is a control weakness a finance director at another council would want to check against their own asset records.
findings.figures: £1m extrapolated net error; £4.2m absolute value of extrapolated errors
findings.quote: Errors in gross internal area data have been reported in the last three ISA260 reports.

findings.headline: The Regulator of Social Housing confirmed the Regulatory Notice issued in March 2024 would be lifted, and gave an overall “C3 consumer grade”.
findings.detail: The Regulator inspected in June and July 2026. The auditor notes that the grade defines serious failings in delivering the consumer standards, and that the Council has a Regulatory Improvement Plan in place.
findings.matters: A lifted regulatory notice alongside a C3 grade is a specific outcome other housing-owning councils can read against their own inspections.
findings.figures: C3 consumer grade
findings.quote: the Regulator confirmed that the Regulatory Notice issued in March 2024 would be lifted, but gave an overall “C3 consumer grade”, which it defines as serious failings in delivering the consumer standards.

findings.headline: If DfE support stays at 90%, the Council estimates a DSG shortfall of between £0.9m and £1.4m would remain at 31 March 2028, after £11.5m to £12m of the residual deficit is met from existing budgets and savings schemes.
findings.detail: The DSG deficit rose to £80.3m at 31 March 2026, mainly due to rising High Needs Block costs. The Council will receive 90% of the 2025/26 residual deficit from the DfE, but support for later years is uncertain.
findings.matters: The DSG deficit and the uncertain DfE support for later years are a live risk for any council under a Safety Valve agreement.
findings.figures: £80.3m DSG deficit at 31 March 2026; 90% DfE support; £0.9m to £1.4m shortfall at 31 March 2028; £11.5m to £12m met from budgets and savings
findings.quote: If the level of support stays at 90%, the Council estimates that a shortfall of between £0.9m and £1.4m would remain at 31 March 2028, after between £11.5m and £12m of the residual deficit is met from existing budgets and savings schemes.

findings.headline: £57.7m of future borrowing has been removed from the capital plan, with a further £30m removed in the October 2026 MTFS report.
findings.detail: The auditor reports these reductions as a response to the rising borrowing forecast. They are part of the Council's medium-term financial planning weakness.
findings.matters: Removing committed capital borrowing is a concrete step that other councils with rising borrowing forecasts can compare against.
findings.figures: £57.7m removed from capital plan; a further £30m in the October 2026 MTFS report
findings.quote: £57.7m of future borrowing has been removed from the capital plan, and a further £30m in the October 2026 MTFS report.

findings.headline: Borrowing is forecast to rise from £817m to £1,048m by March 2029, within the Council’s affordable borrowing limits.
findings.detail: The forecast increase is split between the General Fund (£658m to £790m) and the HRA (£159m to £258m). The auditor notes that the Council has removed some future borrowing from its capital plan.
findings.matters: A forecast rise of about £231m, inside the Council's own limits, is the figure a lender or peer council would compare against its own borrowing trajectory.
findings.figures: £817m borrowing at 2025/26 (GF £658m, HRA £159m); £1,048m forecast by March 2029 (GF £790m, HRA £258m)
findings.quote: Borrowing is forecast to rise from £817m (GF £658m, HRA £159m) to £1,048m (GF £790m, HRA £258m) by March 2029, although it remains within the Council’s affordable borrowing limits.

findings.headline: Kirklees reported a 2025/26 net revenue overspend of £1.8m, after a £21.6m overspend across Adults and Health and Children and Families was covered mainly by savings elsewhere and the £5.5m contingency reserve.
findings.detail: The auditor records that the net overspend fell from £5.6m in 2024/25 to £1.8m in 2025/26. Grant Thornton still treats medium-term financial planning as a significant weakness, and forecasts a significant overspend for 2026/27.
findings.matters: The gross directorate overspend was covered by one-off savings and a contingency draw, which is the pattern a finance director would test against the 2026/27 forecast.
findings.figures: £1.8m net revenue overspend; £21.6m directorate overspend; £5.5m contingency reserve; £5.6m prior-year overspend
findings.quote: In 2025/26 it reported a net revenue overspend of £1.8m, but only after a £21.6m overspend across the Adults and Health and Children and Families directorates was covered mainly by savings elsewhere, many of them one-off, and the £5.5m contingency reserve.

findings.headline: Grant Thornton anticipates an unmodified (‘clean’) opinion on the 2025/26 accounts, so the Council avoids a backstop disclaimer opinion.
findings.detail: The auditor says the audit is substantially complete, subject to listed outstanding matters. The report notes that most other local authorities face a backstop disclaimer, and describes avoiding one as a positive outcome.
findings.matters: A clean opinion on the 2025/26 accounts, when many councils are receiving disclaimers, bears directly on how lenders and peers read the Council's financial reporting.
findings.figures: none
findings.quote: This means the Council avoids a backstop disclaimer opinion, unlike most other local authorities, which is a positive outcome for the Council.

findings.headline: Kirklees Internal Audit is using agency staff to resource key assignments, following concerns about limited resourcing and a low volume of work completed.
findings.detail: The cover report says the committee's September 2026 meeting raised concerns about limited Internal Audit resourcing. As a result, action is in progress to staff key assignments through agency arrangements. The report does not give headcount, cost or the number of assignments affected.
findings.matters: A council's internal audit capacity shapes the assurance it can give on its financial controls, and another council's finance director may be weighing the same resourcing gap against their own audit plan.
findings.figures: None stated in the cover report.
findings.quote: to address concerns about limited resourcing with a consequential low volume of work completed, action is in progress to resource key Internal Audit assignments via Agency staffing arrangements.

findings.paper_title: Treasury Management Mid Year Report 2026-27 FINAL
findings.headline: Investment income for the half-year is £751k, against £1,910k in 2025/26, as the average external balance fell to £39.4m from £89.8m.
findings.detail: The paper attributes the lower average rate of 3.85% (down from 4.21% in the same period last year) to the lower base rate. The LAPF investment of £10.0m generated £201k of dividend income in the period. Investment balances ranged from a peak of £88.4m in June to a low of £27.4m in September.
findings.matters: Falling investment income reduces the offset to treasury costs, and a finance officer at another council can use the same base-rate and balance effects to check their own investment income forecast.
findings.figures: £751k investment income in the period; £1,910k in 2025/26; £39.4 million average external balance (excluding LAPF); £89.8 million in the first six months of 2025/26; 3.85% average rate (4.21% a year earlier); £201k LAPF dividend income
findings.quote: The Council invested an average balance of £39.4 million externally (excluding the

findings.paper_title: Treasury Management Mid Year Report 2026-27 FINAL
findings.headline: The mid-year liability benchmark indicates an underlying requirement for about £70.0m of additional borrowing to support the capital programme.
findings.detail: The paper says the requirement is based on updated capital plans. Appendix 4 shows the liability benchmark rising to £1,077.7m by 31.03.29, against existing borrowing of £560.5m at the same date.
findings.matters: A council that expects to be a long-term borrower with a large gap between its benchmark and existing borrowing has to replace maturing debt and fund new borrowing at current rates, which matters to lenders and to peers with similar gaps.
findings.figures: approximately £70.0 million additional borrowing; £1,077.7m liability benchmark at 31.03.29; £560.5m existing borrowing at 31.03.29
findings.quote: indicates an underlying requirement for approximately £70.0 million of additional borrowing to support the capital programme.

findings.paper_title: Treasury Management Mid Year Report 2026-27 FINAL
findings.headline: Kirklees borrowed £34.0m from other local authorities during the period at a weighted average rate of 4.65%.
findings.detail: The loans run from 9 months to 2 years, and the paper says a mixture of short, medium-term and further PWLB borrowing will be taken during the rest of the year. The treasury budget assumes a borrowing rate of 4.69%, and the paper says actual rates are expected to be higher given market conditions.
findings.matters: Local authority lending at 4.65% sits against PWLB rates that rose during the half-year, so peers and lenders can compare this replacement-funding cost with their own.
findings.figures: £34.0 million borrowed from other local authorities; 4.65% weighted average rate; 4.69% assumed in treasury budget; 10-year PWLB certainty rate 5.62% at 01/04/26 and 6.17% at 30/09/26
findings.quote: £34.0 million of borrowing was undertaken from other local authorities with maturities beyond 2026/27.

findings.paper_title: Treasury Management Mid Year Report 2026-27 FINAL
findings.headline: A lender exercised its option on one of the Council's three £10.0m LOBO loans, and the Council repaid it at no additional cost.
findings.detail: The paper says the revised rate offered was significantly above prevailing borrowing rates, so the Council exercised its option to repay. The loan has not been directly refinanced, and the Council will keep the need for replacement long-term borrowing under review. The paper does not name the lender or state the proposed rate. Appendix 5 records £10,000k of LOBO loans repaid in the period at a weighted average rate of 3.92%.
findings.matters: A call on a LOBO is a repayment-and-replacement event: the council must find the cash, and a finance director here or at another council will want to see whether the replacement funding costs more than the 3.92% coupon that was extinguished.
findings.figures: £10.0 million LOBO called; £10,000k repaid at 3.92% weighted average rate (Appendix 5); £20.0m remaining LOBO balance
findings.quote: The loan was repaid in full at no additional cost and has not been directly refinanced.

findings.paper_title: Treasury Management Mid Year Report 2026-27 FINAL
findings.headline: Forecast net borrowing for 2026/27 is £803.6m, down from £911.0m at the point the strategy was set.
findings.detail: The paper says the reduction is due to slippage in the Capital Plan and confirmation that the Council will receive a High Needs Stability Grant. Table 1 gives the revised forecast at September 2026 as £803.6m net borrowing against a strategy estimate of £911.0m (January 2026).
findings.matters: Lower forecast net borrowing reduces the funding the council needs to find, which is relevant to lenders and to peers planning their own borrowing programmes against the same capital slippage.
findings.figures: £803.6m revised forecast net borrowing (September 2026); £911.0m strategy estimate (January 2026); £786.6m actual at 31 March 2026
findings.quote: forecast net borrowing is now expected to reach £803.6m, down from £911.0 at the point the strategy was set

findings.paper_title: Treasury Management Mid Year Report 2026-27 FINAL
findings.headline: Kirklees forecasts its treasury management budget will be £2.5m under budget against a £40.1m budget for 2026/27 at Q2.
findings.detail: The paper attributes the forecast underspend to slippage in 25/26 and 26/27 borrowing-funded capital expenditure against the February 2026 budget, along with proactive cash management. The forecast underspend was £1m at Q1.
findings.matters: A finance director at another council can compare how much of a treasury budget underspend comes from capital slippage rather than from cash management, since the two have different implications for future borrowing costs.
findings.figures: £40.1 million treasury management budget; £2.5 million forecast underspend at Q2; £1m at Q1
findings.quote: Forecasted outturn is currently under budget by £ 2.5 million

findings.paper_title: Internal Audit and Counter Fraud Q2 26-27 Report
findings.headline: The Committee agreed to replace full audits of primary schools with Limited Assurance with a review of their deficit recovery plans with headteachers, added to the 2026/27 Internal Audit Plan.
findings.detail: Those schools' Limited Assurance opinions reflected their deficit positions, which often rolled forward over several years as pupil rolls fell. The new provision will be undertaken shortly.
findings.matters: Schools' deficits rolling forward across years is a pressure a finance director at another council will recognise, and this paper shows the audit response changing rather than the deficits closing.
findings.figures: no school audits completed in the period
findings.quote: the 2026/27 Internal Audit Plan should be revised to include a separate provision for plans to address the deficit financial position

findings.paper_title: Internal Audit and Counter Fraud Q2 26-27 Report
findings.headline: Internal Audit has eleven planned audits in progress at the end of Q2 2026/27, with ten completed so far this year.
findings.detail: Of the ten completed this year, four received Substantial Assurance, three Adequate, three Limited and none No Assurance. The verbal update to the meeting will report the eleven in progress.
findings.matters: The assurance split across the year gives peers a benchmark, and the paper says the Homes & Neighbourhoods audit work was delayed.
findings.figures: 10 audits completed this year: 4 Substantial, 3 Adequate, 3 Limited, 0 No Assurance; 11 audits in progress
findings.quote: at the end of Q2 2026/27 eleven Planned Audits were in progress towards completion.

findings.paper_title: Internal Audit and Counter Fraud Q2 26-27 Report
findings.headline: Overnight respite care for children is bought from two providers on spot-purchase arrangements totalling almost £0.25m in 2025/26, with no formal contracts in place.
findings.detail: The audit gave Limited Assurance and recommended contracts with all overnight providers, with target completion at the start of November 2026. Invoices were paid at least three months after care was delivered, with around 25% paid more than six months later.
findings.matters: Spend of this size without contracts or timely invoice matching is a payment-control and year-end accrual risk that other councils buying in care will also face.
findings.figures: almost £0.25m spot-purchase spend in 2025/26; all sampled invoices paid at least three months after care delivered; around 25% paid more than six months later
findings.quote: Overnight respite care is currently commissioned from two providers through spot-purchase arrangements totalling almost £0.25m in 2025/26 with no formal contracts in place

findings.paper_title: Internal Audit and Counter Fraud Q2 26-27 Report
findings.headline: Transport Stores received Limited Assurance, with about £1.0 million of annual expenditure not subject to a formal competitive procurement process.
findings.detail: The audit covered Vine Street and George Street depots, with a 2025/26 expenditure budget of £1.06 million. The paper also cites increasing budget overspends and states that the procurement compliance risk remains unresolved pending a long-term purchasing strategy.
findings.matters: A finance director elsewhere will recognise procurement compliance and overspend as a common control gap, and the paper shows the fix depends on a strategy not yet in place.
findings.figures: £1.06 million 2025/26 expenditure budget; approximately £1.0 million of annual expenditure without formal competitive procurement
findings.quote: approximately £1.0 million of annual expenditure not being subject to a formal competitive procurement process

findings.headline: Kirklees Council reports a 2025/26 Annual Governance Statement with no change in the level of control issues, and overall assurance levels improved over 2024/25.
findings.detail: The Head of Audit's annual assurance opinion says control issues were similar to previous years, with assurance levels improving. Concerns persist in contract management, data and information management, and cash handling.
findings.matters: Persisting concerns in cash handling and contract management are control weaknesses a finance director will want to check against their own internal audit findings.
findings.figures: not stated in figures
findings.quote: The incidence of control issues was similar to previous years, although overall assurance levels had improved over 2024/25.

findings.headline: Kirklees external auditor issued an unqualified opinion on the 2024/25 financial statements, with three VFM key recommendations carried forward.
findings.detail: The paper notes the external auditor recorded positive improvements in the Council's overall financial position and expected these to be reflected in the 2025/26 VFM report. Financial sustainability, SEND and housing regulatory issues remain identified as valid by the auditor at the end of 2025/26.
findings.matters: A finance director reading VFM recommendations and an unqualified opinion will want to compare how the auditor is treating financial sustainability and SEND at their own authority.
findings.figures: three key recommendations retained from the previous year
findings.quote: The 2024/25 financial statements, approved in January 2026, received an unqualified opinion

findings.headline: Kirklees received £42m of revenue savings agreed for 2024/25 and a balanced budget for 2025/26, both cited as the basis for closing the 2023/24 financial stability issue.
findings.detail: The paper reports the earlier financial stability issue as complete in 2024/25 because of these actions. It describes the future financial sustainability issue as still open for 2026/27 and beyond.
findings.matters: A finance director can compare the scale of the 2024/25 savings package and the route the council took to close its earlier stability issue.
findings.figures: £42m revenue savings agreed for 2024/25; savings of £21.8m tracked monthly
findings.quote: including the agreement of £42m revenue savings for 2024/25, a balanced budget for 2025/26

findings.headline: Kirklees housing service received a C3 judgement from the Regulator following a summer 2026 inspection, replacing the March 2024 Regulatory Notice.
findings.detail: The paper says the judgement identified serious failings principally in stock condition and decency and anti-social behaviour. A service improvement plan with financial and operational resources identified is now in place, and the Council remains subject to regulatory scrutiny.
findings.matters: Regulatory judgements on housing stock, with financial resources attached to the improvement plan, are a cost and reputational exposure that lenders and finance directors at other housing authorities will track.
findings.figures: C3 judgement; fire door and compartmentation contracts awarded October 2026; completion anticipated by February 2028 for the low-rise programme
findings.quote: Following the inspection in summer 2026, the Council received a C3 judgement, which replaced the March 2024 Regulatory Notice.

findings.headline: Kirklees MTFS budget gap for 2027/28 was £24m, with draft budget proposals stated to have addressed it in the main, subject to February 2027 approval.
findings.detail: The paper says the draft budget proposals have in the main addressed the £24m gap, subject to Council approval in February 2027. The draft 2027/28 budget with new savings proposals goes to Cabinet in December 2026.
findings.matters: A finance director will want to see how the 2027/28 gap is being closed and whether the savings proposals land at the February 2027 budget meeting.
findings.figures: budget gap per MTFS for 27/28 was £24m
findings.quote: The budget gap per the MTFS for 27/28 was £24m. The draft budget proposals have in the main addressed these – subject to Council budget approval in February 2027.

findings.headline: Kirklees reduced its 2026/27 capital plan from an initial £315m to £262.3m in the MTFS refresh.
findings.detail: The paper says the capital plan was revised down as part of the MTFS refresh, and that ongoing review is ensuring the programme remains affordable. A sustainable capital plan is being developed for the December budget report.
findings.matters: A council cutting its capital programme by about £52.7m during the year is a signal finance officers elsewhere will want to track, both for affordability and for borrowing needs.
findings.figures: initial budgeted expenditure £315m (General Fund plus HRA); revised to £262.3m in MTFS refresh
findings.quote: The 2026/27 capital plan had an initial budgeted expenditure of £315m (General Fund plus Housing Revenue Account). This was revised down to £262.3m in the MTFS refresh.

findings.headline: Kirklees projected a £9.8m overspend at Q2 2026/27 and delivered 59% of planned savings in-year.
findings.detail: The paper states the projected overspend was considered in the October 2026 MTFP refresh. It also notes that the 2026/27 budget provided significant additional funding for demand pressures and overspending services, which is expected to reduce in-year variations.
findings.matters: Savings delivery at 59% at mid-year and a £9.8m projected overspend are measures a finance director can benchmark against their own in-year savings and variance tracking.
findings.figures: projected overspend £9.8m at Q2; savings delivery 59% of planned savings in year; savings of £21.8m tracked monthly
findings.quote: The projected overspend of £9.8m at the end of Q2 has been considered as part of the MTFP refresh in October 2026. Savings delivery at Q2 is 59% of the planned savings being achieved in year.

findings.headline: Kirklees DSG SEND deficit stood at £81.3m at 31 March 2026, up from £63.8m at 31 March 2025, with a £73m High Needs Stability Grant payment expected in November 2026.
findings.detail: The paper reports that the Safety Valve programme is no longer the primary framework and that the DfE will pay off 90% of the DSG deficit through the High Needs Stability Grant. The Council is responsible for the remaining 10%, which must be eradicated by March 2028 when the statutory override ends.
findings.matters: A finance director at another council with a DSG deficit will want to compare the 90% DfE contribution terms and the March 2028 override deadline against their own position.
findings.figures: deficit £81.3m at 31/3/26; £63.8m at 31/3/25; £73m grant expected November 2026; in-year deficit for 2026/27 projected at £29m at Q2; c £4m pa cost to General Fund
findings.quote: The deficit at 31st March 2026 was £81.3m (£63.8m at 31/3/25).

findings.headline: Internal Audit's sample review of risk management in the Place Directorate gave an assessment of 'Adequate Assurance'
findings.detail: The paper says that Internal Audit reviewed risk management arrangements in the Place Directorate on a sample basis this year. The resulting assessment was Adequate Assurance. The report does not give findings for other directorates, and it describes the risk management process as overly manual, so the risk of error or omission may persist.
findings.matters: An internal audit assurance grade for risk management is a formal, comparable signal of control quality that finance officers and external auditors read alongside the council's own self-assessment.
findings.quote: This year, Internal Audit reviewed arrangements for risk management within the Place Directorate on a sample basis, with a resulting assessment of Adequate Assurance.

findings.headline: Kirklees has no Risk Appetite Statement, and a draft is to be re-consulted on and taken through governance approval in 2026-27
findings.detail: The paper describes the absence of a Risk Appetite Statement as a recognised gap in the framework. A draft was developed with officers and previous members and was shared with this Committee with the 2024-25 report. The risk team will re-engage senior officers and members on the draft before it goes through governance.
findings.matters: A council without a stated risk appetite has no formal basis for judging whether a proposed decision sits inside or outside the risk it is willing to take, which is a common gap finance directors are asked to close.
findings.quote: The absence of a Risk Appetite Statement is a recognised gap within the Council RMF.

findings.headline: Kirklees added 'Economic growth and regeneration' to its corporate risk report in Q1 2025-26 and 'Sufficiency of Children’s Care' in Q3 2025-26
findings.detail: The paper lists two risks removed from the corporate risk report in Q1 2025-26, the Adult social care assurance framework and Data insight for operational delivery of adult social care. It records two additions in the same year: Economic growth and regeneration, raised in Q1 2025-26, and Sufficiency of Children’s Care, raised in Q3 2025-26.
findings.matters: Escalating a children's care sufficiency risk to corporate level, and removing adult social care risks in the same year, shows which service pressures a council's leadership is treating as strategic.
findings.figures: Two risks removed and two raised, with the corporate total held at 24
findings.quote: Sufficiency of Children’s Care (raised in Q3 2025-26)

findings.headline: The number of Red-rated risks on Kirklees' corporate risk report fell from nine at Q4 2024-25 to two at Q4 2025-26
findings.detail: The paper reports that the council's risk profile improved over 2025-26, with the number of Red-rated risks falling from nine to two. It names the two remaining risks as SI03 Cyber Security (score 16) and LGC02 Data processing and Access to information (score 15). The total number of corporate risks stayed constant at 24.
findings.matters: A falling count of Red-rated corporate risks is a visible, comparable measure of how a council's risk exposure is moving, and peers can benchmark their own profiles against it.
findings.figures: Red-rated risks: nine (Q4 2024-25) to two (Q4 2025-26), in a corporate risk report of 24 risks; SI03 Cyber Security score 16 (Likelihood 4 x Impact 4); LGC02 score 15 (Likelihood 5 x Impact 3)
findings.quote: the risk profile of the council has significantly improved with the number of risks scored as a ‘Red’ rated risk reduced from nine to two.

findings.headline: The sensitivity analysis places the 2027/28 deficit between £22.5m and £30.6m, and the 2031/32 deficit between £62.4m and £96.3m
findings.detail: The paper's best and worst case scenarios sit around the base position of £24.0m in 2027/28 and £67.8m in 2031/32. It says the MTFS figures remain at the optimistic end of the sensitivities.
findings.matters: The width of the scenario range shows how sensitive a council's gap is to assumptions on inflation, funding and demand, which peers use to test their own sensitivity.

findings.headline: The Recovery Grant of £8.4m is assumed flat across the plan but has not been confirmed by Government beyond 2028/29

findings.headline: High Needs Block deficit of £82.2m at March 2026 now 90% funded by government through High Needs Stability Grant with council responsible for 10%
findings.detail: The cumulative High Needs Block deficit reached £82.2m at 31 March 2026, with an annual deficit of £17m in 2025/26 (an improvement of £3m from prior year). The statutory override allowing DSG deficit balance sheet recognition ends March 2028.

Disposal transfers this liability to the new owner and removes the council's requirement to undertake an extended remediation programme.
findings.matters: Converting a known future liability into a present capital receipt improves the council's financial position and removes exposure to ongoing remediation costs.
